Reproduce the Greater Bangkok study

RStudio workflow, input provenance and analytical checks

Author

Zhenhua Liu

Exercise home · Technical report · Executive summary

1. Open the existing R project

Clone or download the coursework repository, then open ISSS626-GAA.Rproj in RStudio. Run all commands from the website root. Keep the exercise folder named exactly take home exercise1; spaces in its path are intentional.

This study uses R 4.5.3 and Quarto 1.10.18 on Windows. The report records the exact package versions and spatial libraries in sessionInfo().

needed <- c("sf", "dplyr", "readr", "ggplot2", "spatstat.geom",
            "spatstat.explore", "spatstat.random", "knitr", "rmarkdown",
            "jsonlite", "digest")
missing <- setdiff(needed, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing)) install.packages(missing, repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
source("take home exercise1/R/check-environment.R")

No Python, alternative statistical platform or road-network package is needed for this analytical workflow.

2. Acquire and verify the inputs

source("take home exercise1/R/download-data.R")

The downloader retrieves the Kaggle archive and a version-pinned geoBoundaries GeoJSON. It verifies SHA-256 hashes against the committed manifest, and stops on mismatches. It reuses existing matching files. Internet access is needed only for missing inputs.

If Kaggle’s public endpoint is unavailable, download the original dataset archive from its source page, place it in take home exercise1/data/raw/ under the filename in the manifest, and rerun the helper. Do not change a reference checksum just to bypass a mismatch: a new source version requires a fresh validation.

The accident dataset is listed as CC0; administrative boundaries are ODbL 1.0, attributed to geoBoundaries, OpenStreetMap contributors and Wambacher. Raw files are downloaded separately to keep the repository manageable. The site redistributes figures as attributed produced works, not an edited boundary database.

3. Run the complete analysis and render

The report executes the preparation and analysis scripts in order, regenerates every figure and table, and displays the corresponding code. Render through R:

source("take home exercise1/R/render.R")

This builds the entire website and updates its navigation. Existing frozen results from earlier exercises are reused; the take-home report is executed on each build. A report-only refresh is also available:

system2(Sys.which("quarto"),
        c("render", shQuote("take home exercise1/technical-report.qmd")))

To inspect intermediate R objects interactively before rendering:

source("take home exercise1/R/prepare.R")
source("take home exercise1/R/analysis.R")

The script order matters: analysis.R uses objects created by prepare.R. A full clean repository build may also require the input downloads documented in the earlier exercises’ READMEs. The take-home report itself needs only the two source datasets described here.

4. Understand the files and outputs

File or directory Role
technical-report.qmd Executed report; reads labelled sections with knitr::read_chunk()
executive-summary.qmd Quarto revealjs presentation; reuses the same R-generated figures
R/prepare.R Validation, 2022 restriction, spatial selection, audit and overview map
R/analysis.R Monthly rates, KDE, simulations, sensitivity and remaining figures
R/download-data.R Downloads and verifies original inputs
R/check-environment.R Verifies all required packages and Quarto
R/render.R Builds the website from R
data/metadata/ Committed source metadata and checksum manifest
data/raw/ Original inputs, downloaded locally and ignored by Git
data/derived/ Regenerated audit tables, statistical tables and summary JSON
figures/ Five generated PNG figures committed for the report and slides

The final HTML pages and shared assets are written to _site/, following the existing site’s publishing structure. Scripts and metadata linked from the report are copied as website resources. Raw and intermediate data are excluded from website deployment.

5. Check the reproduced results

For the pinned input versions, the workflow should produce:

Check Expected result
Original CSV records 81,735
2022 records 21,032
Geolocated events inside the six-province window 3,599
Distinct recorded coordinate pairs 3,278
Fatal accidents / recorded deaths 159 / 177
Global conditional CSR p-value 0.005
Global one-sided stratified fatal-pair p-value 0.998

The four simulation seeds are 6262022, 6262023, 6262024 and 6262025. CSR uses 199 simulations; fatal-label comparisons use 999 permutations. Package-version differences can affect numerical details, so compare the input hashes, package versions, point counts and assumptions before interpreting changed results.

Every major visual has its own interpretation of fewer than 150 words. The planning discussion is under 500 words. The presentation contains ten content slides plus cover and contents. Source code, figures and rendered pages should be committed together when updating the site.

6. Publication routes

  • Technical report
  • Executive summary
  • GitHub exercise folder

Netlify publishes the existing site’s _site/ output. The GitHub source is on main. Verify the live pages and their figures after a deployment; a successful local render alone does not confirm an online publication.
